faq.q: What should I wear when it is hot?
faq.a: Wear light, loose clothes made of cotton, a sun hat and sunglasses, and put on sun cream. Drink plenty of water too.

faq.q: Why do we wear layers when it is cold?
faq.a: Each layer traps a thin blanket of air, and still air is very good at keeping your body heat in. Several thin layers keep you warmer than one, and you can take one off if you get hot.
asks: How do clothes keep you warm?

faq.q: How do I know what the weather will be?
faq.a: Look at the sky, and check a weather forecast on the radio, TV or a phone. Forecasters use satellites, weather balloons and computers to predict the weather.

faq.q: Why do we wear sun cream?
faq.a: Sunlight contains invisible rays called ultraviolet rays that can burn your skin. Sun cream blocks many of them, even on cloudy days.
asks: Can you get sunburnt on a cloudy day?

faq.q: Why are raincoats made of plastic or rubber?
faq.a: Plastic and rubber are waterproof: rain cannot soak through them, so they keep you and your clothes dry.

facts: Weather satellites orbit the Earth and photograph clouds and storms to help forecasters.
Layers of clothing keep you warm by trapping still air, a good insulator.

quiz.say: It is snowing outside. Which should you wear?
quiz.why: A woolly hat and gloves trap warm air and keep you warm in the cold.

wrong.1: Shorts would leave you freezing in the snow.
wrong.2: A T-shirt alone is far too cold for snow.

quiz.say: Why does an umbrella help on a rainy day?
quiz.show: An umbrella helps because it is…
quiz.why: An umbrella is waterproof, so rain runs off it.

wrong.1: An umbrella keeps you dry, not warm.
wrong.2: Some umbrellas are see-through, but that is not what keeps you dry.
